newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian credibility at stake over IRI - Van Miert.
newsitem.headline: Italian credibility at stake over IRI - Van Miert.

text.p: The credibility of the Italian government is at stake over the sale of telecoms group Stet and the reduction of debt at state holding IRI, European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert said on Monday.
Under a 1993 deal, Italy assured the European Commission it would cut IRI's debt to below five trillion lire ($3.3 billion) by the end of 1996, compared with 22.46 trillion at end-1995.

The only way to approach that figure is by selling Stet, but legislation needed for the privatisation has been snarled in parliament and the government has won a six-month extension to the original timetable.
However there are increasing worries in government circles that even this new deadline might be missed.
"The government's credibility is at stake," Van Miert told reporters after attending a conference at Genoa university.
He said that although both Prime Minister Romano Prodi and Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi were committed to reducing IRI's debt level, there were still problems.
"I want to ring the alarm bells," he said.

Legislation covering the creation of a telecoms watchdog body, seen as essential to the Stet sell-off, has been snowed under by thousands of amendments in parliament with a key government ally, the hard left Communist Refoundation, ideologically opposed to the privatisation.
